Stated Claim / Post Context:
Police, airport prepare for President Trump’s Grand Island visit

Grand Island Police Department, Central Nebraska Regional Airport preparing for President Trump's Monday arrival.

Actual Article Body:
GRAND ISLAND, Neb. (KSNB) - Law enforcement is preparing for President Donald Trump’s arrival in Grand Island on Monday.

The Grand Island Police Department is working with county, state and federal agencies to prepare for the visit.

Chief Kevin Denney said communication and preparations have gone well so far. The arrival will result in overtime costs for officers helping with event security.

Denney said the process will require all hands on deck for the department.

“We’re going to pull in our police officers for the minimal amount of time that we need them and we’re going to track that overtime as we go, so we’ll have a more specific number after Monday, but we’re going to track the officers overtime, so in addition to the officers working Monday, we’ll be calling in the other officers on their day off to help supplement us,” Denney said.

The police department is working with the Secret Service over the weekend to prepare for the president’s arrival.

Overtime costs to affect city and surrounding areas

Denney said one drawback to the arrival is that it will come at a cost to the city and some of the surrounding areas because of overtime.

“About half of the officers are not even Grand Island officers, so half the officers are other assets from other departments, or from other sheriff’s offices or from the State Patrol, so everybody is having some of the burden on this and it is going to be tracked, so we will know how much this event’s going to cost us,” Denney said.

Denney said despite the cost, things have gone well so far and there has been a lot of communication between state and federal law enforcement.

“There’s a lot of communication between the various law enforcement entities, as well as other entities within the city and the state regarding other resources that we need, so a lot of planning, a lot of logistics, but everything is going very smoothly and we’re all working very well together,” Denney said.

Airport to restrict airspace

Officials at the Central Nebraska Regional Airport said the airspace will be restricted once President Trump arrives. They said it will not affect commercial air traffic throughout the day. Officials could not comment on when the airspace restriction would take effect or what time the president is set to arrive Monday.
